title: Brokered SLA Lanes & GPU Commitment Policy Worksheet
creator: Asha Patel
description: Consolidate an operational rubric that maps incoming enterprise dedicated-capacity requests into a brokered SLA lane, including reserved throughput envelopes, GPU class recommendations, and autoscale/eviction policies. This worksheet captures intake signal thresholds, decision rules for assigning 'gold/silver/bronze' SLA lanes, trade-offs, and handoff steps for capacity provisioning and contracting.
background: We see repeated bespoke enterprise asks where teams want both predictable latency SLOs and burst throughput without over-committing GPUs. Existing playbooks are fragmented across Confluence pages and stale. Customers are lost in configuration choices (GPU family, reserved qps, burst credits) and SEs escalate to Eng for every nuance. This initiative aims to centralize a decision-grade worksheet usable by PMs/SEs/Customer Success during intake.
goals: Define deterministic routing rules that map measurable workload signals to SLA lanes
Produce GPU-class recommendation rules (e.g., 80% of peak qps -> A100; throughput-centric -> H100/Trn) with clear cost trade-offs
Standardize reserved throughput agreements and burst credit definitions
Create an operational handoff checklist that triggers Dedicated pool provisioning and legal/finance templates
scope: Design the rubric, validation criteria, and a one-page intake worksheet for SEs/PMs. Draft accompanying API/console flags to reflect SLA lane selection. Coordinate with ENG for feasibility of autoscale and preemption rules.
out_of_scope: Implementation of provisioning automation and final contract language; detailed cost modeling for every GPU SKU (high-level guidance only).
success_metrics: Reduce engineering clarifying questions during intake by 60% (tracked via SE survey)
Time from initial customer request to Dedicated pool provision start reduced to <= 7 business days
>80% reproducible mapping of requests into SLA lanes without ad-hoc exceptions
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed worksheet and rubric approved by PM, 2 SEs, and Head of Dedicated Capacity
Pilot intake used in at least 3 real customer requests and feedback captured
Dependencies (ENG-49221 autoscale policy stubs) identified and assigned
decisions: Adopt three SLA lanes: Gold (99.9% p99 latency SLO, reserved pool), Silver (90th percentile latency SLO, mixed reserved/burst), Bronze (best-effort burst-only)
Map workload fingerprints to GPU family guidance rather than strict enforcement (recommendation matrix with fallback rules)
Define 'burst credit' as a short-term, measurable extra qps allowance tied to a throttling window (default 30 minutes)
tradeoffs: Conservative reserved throughput reduces risk but increases cost/capital for customers
Aggressive packing onto lower-tier GPUs lowers cost but complicates fallbacks when latency spikes
Strict SLO enforcement requires deeper observability (cost/time to build) vs. looser guidance which risks inconsistent customer outcomes
